- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — especially if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply lagged smoothing or dampen momentum.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: model often fails to capture gradual pullback after sharp rises; use recent 7-14d average as baseline for correction.
- Forecasts with high sentiment volatility (rapid swings) show higher error; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing or reduce forecast variance in such cases.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 3 consecutive days, model likely missed a bullish breakout — increase forecast by 1-2% for next period if sentiment remains positive.
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome by >3% over 5+ days, model may be underestimating sentiment-driven momentum — adjust upward by 0.5-1.5% per day if sentiment remains positive.
